title: minimize-observability-hotpath-locks-and-introduce-stream-encoder
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce CPU and allocation pressure in the runtime observability hot path by removing coarse-grained locks, replacing allocation-heavy JSON span encoding with a streaming compact encoder, and adding a lightweight bypass for non-critical telemetry. This ticket implements a lock-free ring buffer for span events, a thin fastpath that avoids the full OpenTelemetry SDK for high-throughput internals, and upgrades the Otel SDK to 1.24.0 to take advantage of recent batching and exporter fixes. The goal is to lower per-request CPU for inference-serving processes and decrease tail latency caused by observability flushes.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end CPU usage for the runtime process reduced by >=20% under the reference loadbench (same model, 4k sequence distribution)
P99 request latency attributable to observability work reduced by >=25ms in realistic canary traffic
Span and metric delivery rate maintained within 99% of baseline for critical telemetry (errors, request traces) after rollout; non-critical diagnostics may be sampled or dropped
Feature-flagged rollout path exists (off by default) with canary percentages and automatic rollback on increased error rate or span loss above thresholds
Automated unit and integration tests covering ring buffer concurrency, encoder correctness, and fallback to synchronous exporter on OOM or trace sink failure
Migration doc and runbook added with links to dashboard panels and playbook steps for rollback and debugging
comments: 2026-02-10 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes attached in Confluence. Agreed scope: lock removal (hotpath), streaming encoder, Otel SDK upgrade. Will keep legacy path behind feature flag for 2-week canary.

2026-02-12 - Marco Ruiz: Prototype ring buffer implemented. Microbenchmarks show 30% fewer allocations for span emit in synthetic harness. Pushed branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/obs/lockfree-ringbuf

2026-02-15 - SRE (Evan Ng): Raised concern about span ordering with lock-free buffer; suggested sequence slot validation and a small per-producer sequence counter to detect reordering. Added as follow-up in design doc.

2026-02-18 - Marco Ruiz: Upgraded OpenTelemetry SDK to v1.24.0 in feature branch. Verified compatibility with our exporter interface; had to adjust BatchSpanProcessor config to match new backpressure knobs. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/13456

2026-02-20 - Design review (Lina Gomez): Approved streaming encoder layout; requested compact binary option be toggled off by default for interoperability. We'll keep JSON compact as default and enable binary via org-level config.
2026-02-24 - QA (Ravi Shah): Integration test failures fixed (race condition in buffer drain). Added additional assertions to ensure no span loss when exporter temporarily returns 429.

2026-02-28 - Marco Ruiz: Canary plan drafted. Initial canary: 2% traffic for 24h, monitor 'spans_dropped_total' and 'obs_flush_latency_seconds'. If thresholds exceeded, automatic rollback will trigger. Playbook link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFR/pages/Obs+Hotpath+Rollout
